mutants.description: soft_start's ramp branch is enabled only while the ramp is unfinished (ss_active and not SS_done), as if a finished ramp no longer needed the S_SS branch, so on the last S_SS clock it falls into the reset-to-floor branch
mutants.reason: On the clock after SS_done sets, the supervisor is still in S_SS, so soft_start resets max_on_counts to the 12-clock floor and clears SS_done while the FSM moves to S_RUN. soft_start then holds that floor through S_RUN, and PWM_out is cut to the floor on-time for the whole run instead of the max_on_limit ceiling.

mutants.description: fault_arbiter is handed the soft-start trip threshold minus one, as if it tripped on count > trip_ss, though it already compares with >=
mutants.reason: In S_SS, window_trip_SS and the S_SS -> S_HICCUP exit (En dropping) now fire when 27 of the last 32 valley samples are faulted instead of 28. A host-written TRIP_SS is also one cycle short.

mutants.description: fault_cause is held in reset while the gate driver is disabled, so routine power-downs do not log a fault. This wipes the record on every fault shutdown, which is exactly when it must survive.
mutants.reason: A fault in S_SS or S_RUN drops En at once (combinationally for OTP, UVLO and latch, or by entering S_HICCUP or S_OFF), so the cause captured on that clock is cleared. FAULT_REG and FAULT_TIME read back zero over SPI after any shutdown, instead of holding the cause until the host reads it.

mutants.description: fault_LED's over-temperature input is gated by 'converter running' like fault_cause's capture gate, though the LEDs show what is wrong now and must light in any state
mutants.reason: When OTP asserts in S_RUN the supervisor goes to S_OFF on the next clock, so Red_LED2 lights for at most a clock and then stays dark while the board is still over-temperature. With OTP present in S_OFF it never lights at all.
